visual_goal: Show the Borrowed Roadmap as a vicious loop (vendor decisions shape architecture, dependencies grow, negotiating power falls) and an enterprise-owned target state and vendor strategy breaking it.
prompt: Center-left of the picture: a circular loop of four stations connected by four thick orange curved arrows going clockwise: at the top a generic unbranded office tower labeled 'Vendor decisions'; at the right a set of building blocks labeled 'Architecture choices'; at the bottom a tangle of chains labeled 'Dependencies'; at the left a tilted balance scale labeled 'Negotiating power'. Inside the loop a small label 'Borrowed Roadmap'. At the far left edge of the picture, directly left of 'Negotiating power', a calendar page labeled 'Renewal', with one short blue arrow pointing right from 'Renewal' into the balance scale. At the far right, a flag on a hill labeled 'Target state', with one blue arrow pointing left into a shield labeled 'Vendor strategy'. From 'Vendor strategy' exactly two blue arrows: one pointing left into 'Architecture choices', with a small funnel icon on it; and one long blue arrow that rises and runs along the very top edge of the picture, over the whole loop, and comes down at the far left into the 'Renewal' calendar. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: A clockwise orange loop from vendor decisions to architecture choices, dependencies and falling negotiating power, labeled the Borrowed Roadmap, with an enterprise target state and vendor strategy filtering choices and preparing renewals that restore negotiating power.

visual_goal: Show exit-plan maturity as four rising stages, with a drop back from Tested to Estimated when scope or contract changes and an annual re-test loop.
prompt: A staircase of four rising steps from left to right, each step a block labeled: 'Named', 'Documented', 'Estimated', 'Tested'. One small upward arrow between each consecutive step. 'Named' shows a small signpost, 'Documented' a document stack, 'Estimated' a calculator, 'Tested' a green checkmark on a database cylinder. A short curved orange arrow starts on the 'Tested' block and lands on the 'Estimated' block right next to it, the step immediately below, labeled 'contract or scope change'. A small circular arrow sits on top of 'Tested', labeled 'annual re-test'. Exactly five arrows.
alt: A staircase of exit-plan maturity from Named to Documented, Estimated and Tested, with an annual re-test loop on Tested and an arrow dropping back to Estimated when contract or scope changes.

visual_goal: Show where Northmere places enterprise-owned boundaries: adapters in front of payments, tax and e-invoicing, an event backbone in front of finance tools, while the general ledger is used directly and bank connectivity relies on a standard file format.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration. At the far left a box 'Brand platforms'. Next, a vertical column of three thick blue protective walls with plug sockets, labeled top to bottom 'Payment adapters', 'Tax adapter', 'Event backbone'; one arrow from 'Brand platforms' into each wall. Behind 'Payment adapters' on the right, a group of three small plain generic boxes labeled once 'Payment providers'. Behind 'Tax adapter', a plain box labeled 'Tax engine'. From 'Event backbone' one arrow right into a large open book labeled 'General ledger' (no wall in front of it) and one arrow into a box labeled 'Reconciliation'. From 'General ledger', one arrow to a box labeled 'Consolidation'; one arrow to a thick blue protective wall labeled 'E-invoicing gateway' with a box behind it labeled 'E-invoicing provider'; and one arrow carrying a standard file icon labeled 'ISO 20022' to a box labeled 'Treasury'. Plugs and walls are blue; vendor boxes are grey.
alt: Brand platforms reach payment providers, the tax engine and finance tools through enterprise-owned adapters and an event backbone; the general ledger is used directly, feeding consolidation, an e-invoicing gateway and treasury via a standard ISO 20022 file.
